ELI5: Why is gas so cheap in the US?

Europe discourages gasoline consumption to reduce vehicular traffic and promote mass transit, bicycles and walking- which are all usable since Europe is densely populated. Diesel is cheap in Europe because it can be run in efficient small engine vehicles and produce reasonably less emissions. In the US, gasoline is cheaper because we have oil production capabilities, large oil and gas reserves, significant refinery capacity and efficient pipeline systems that allow for cheap and easy transport all around the country. Driving gasoline vehicles is a necessity in most areas since the US is less densely populated outside of large urban cities and long range mass transit is less practical or completely unavailable. Diesel is more costly because most passenger vehicles are only available in gasoline powered varieties. The US' love affair with powerful and fast vehicles means more demand for fuel so prices will reflect the balance between production and demand. US refineries will produce less diesel and more gasoline for this reason. Unlike most European nations, the US has everything it needs to produce and distribute gasoline domestically and have major influence on the world oil and gas economy and production. All these things combine to make gasoline cheaper in the US. This is probably not ELI5 but I'm sure it comes across easily.
